pc-d1:
A $50k ACV security product is usually bought through a security VAR, an MSSP, or a cloud marketplace. This program covers referral and resale partners. MSSPs need multi-tenant licensing and different economics, so give them their own track once that licensing exists.

## Start with the economics

I set tier values by comparing each partner motion with selling direct, not by copying a competitor's program page. With illustrative inputs (10% rep commission, $18k of direct presales and marketing per deal, lower acquisition cost on partner deals, 20% cost to serve, 90% renewal, 3-year view):

- **Direct:** about $85k of 3-year contribution per $50k deal
- **Referral:** a one-time fee matches direct up to about **14%** of first-year revenue
- **Resale:** a discount matches direct only up to about **9 points**, because it recurs at every renewal

Referral fees are cheap. A 20–25% resale discount only pays on deals you couldn't have reached yourself. That's why the bigger discount is tied to approved registrations on net-new deals, and why it steps down at renewal. Put your real numbers in before launch.

## The tiers (starting values to test, not benchmarks)

| | Registered | Silver | Gold |
|---|---|---|---|
| **For** | Advisors and VARs trying you out | VARs with a security practice | Partners who sell, deploy, and support without your engineers |
| **Requirements** | Signed agreement; anti-corruption and sanctions screening passed; 1 sales-certified person | 2 certified sellers, 1 certified engineer; signed joint business plan (JBP); $150k trailing-12-month partner-sourced bookings or 3 closed deals | 4 certified sellers, 3 certified engineers; $500k trailing-12-month sourced bookings or 8 deals; deployment CSAT at or above target; named executive sponsor |
| **Referral fee** | 10% of first-year revenue, paid once after the customer pays | 12% | 14% |
| **Resale, new logo** | Not offered | 10% base + 10 points on approved registration | 15% base + 10 points on approved registration |
| **Resale, renewal** | n/a | 10% if the partner still supports the customer | 15%, same condition |
| **MDF** | None | Proposal-based, pre-approved, paid on proof of performance | Allocated in the JBP, same proof rule |
| **Enablement** | Self-paced sales course, portal, deal registration | Technical certification, NFR licenses for labs and demos, SE help on proofs of value | Named partner manager, SE coverage, roadmap briefings |
| **Co-marketing** | Directory listing after first closed deal | Case studies, campaign kits | Joint events and campaigns funded under the JBP |
| **Tier review** | Annual | Semi-annual | Quarterly |

## The rules that make it work

1. **Deal registration.** The first complete, valid registration wins. Decide within 2 business days, with a reason code. Protection lasts 90 days, with one 60-day extension on documented progress, because security proofs of value run long. A deal already open for direct isn't eligible. Disputes get a written appeal path.
2. **Comp-neutral AEs.** Direct reps are paid the same on partner-registered deals, and that cost is already in the economics. Taking a registered deal direct is a policy violation.
3. **Definitions agreed with RevOps before launch.** Partner-sourced needs a registration timestamp that predates any open opportunity. Partner-influenced is reported next to the sourced number, never added to it.
4. **Resellers set their own prices.** Publish a suggested price only, and have counsel review pricing clauses.
5. **Due diligence before signing,** deeper for partners selling to government. Red flags: extra-discount requests with no competitive reason, payments to third-country accounts, MDF claims without invoices or attendee lists. Findings go to counsel.
6. **Prune on a calendar.** Partners who miss tier criteria move down with the notice the agreement requires. A partner with no registered deal in 12 months is offboarded.

## Marketplaces

Plenty of security buyers want to draw down an AWS or Azure commitment. List there, and let Silver and Gold resellers use reseller-led private offers (AWS Channel Partner Private Offers, Microsoft multiparty private offers). Add the provider's fee to the discount in your model, using the current published figure and the date you checked it. Finance decides gross versus net reporting.

## Measure from day one

- Days from signing to first closed deal, by recruit cohort
- Share of partners with a closed deal in the trailing 12 months
- Win rate and cycle on registered deals versus direct in the same segment
- Contribution per motion, recomputed quarterly with actuals

Recruit 8–10 partners scored against an ideal partner profile, not whoever fills in a sign-up form. Send me your direct cost of sale, rep comp plan, and how your last 20 wins bought (VAR, MSSP, marketplace, or direct). I'll rerun the numbers and we'll see whether these discounts hold.
pc-d2:
Spend the first 90 days making the reseller able to sell, not on a launch announcement. The plan runs on three dated milestones: first certified seller (day 30), signed joint business plan (day 45), first registered deal (day 60).

## Before day 1: gates, not tasks

Nothing below starts until these are done:

- **Signed, non-exclusive agreement** with anti-corruption, audit, termination, and customer transition clauses. If they ask for exclusivity in Germany, trade it only for written performance commitments.
- **Due diligence and sanctions screening** passed, deeper if they sell to the public sector.
- **Data-sharing terms** approved by counsel and your privacy lead. GDPR applies, so account mapping starts at company level. Contact-level data waits for a written lawful basis.
- **EUR price list with suggested prices only.** The reseller sets its own prices. EU competition law treats resale price maintenance as a hardcore restriction, so pricing clauses go to counsel.
- **VAT, invoicing, and payment terms** confirmed with Finance and a tax adviser.
- **Rules of engagement with your direct team** if you have DACH reps: the written deal registration policy, and AEs paid the same on partner deals.

## Days 1–30: Enable and map

**Milestone: 2 certified sellers and 1 certified technical person.**

- Kickoff with an executive sponsor on each side. Name the partner's practice lead and the sellers who'll carry your product.
- PRM access and a deal registration walkthrough: what's eligible, who wins, approval SLA, protection window, appeal path.
- Sales certification for named sellers, technical certification started, and NFR licenses so they can demo and run a lab.
- German-language sales kit: pitch deck, one-pager, pricing guide, and the documents German buyers ask for early (DPA, hosting location, ISO 27001, and BSI C5 if you sell cloud services to the public sector).
- Account mapping under NDA at company level. Shortlist 15–20 overlap accounts.
- Order-to-cash dry run: quote, order, EUR invoice, provisioning. Find the gaps before a customer does.

## Days 31–60: Plan and pipeline

**Milestones: signed joint business plan by day 45, first registered deal by day 60.**

- Write the JBP: why customers buy the joint offer, 8–10 named accounts with an owner on each side and a dated next step, certification targets, and 6- and 12-month pipeline and bookings targets.
- Your SE leads the first two or three customer meetings. The partner's engineer co-leads the next ones.
- Run one small German-language campaign for the shortlist, such as a webinar or roundtable. MDF only if pre-approved, and paid against invoices and attendee lists.
- Decide every registration within the SLA, with a reason code. A partner whose first registration sits in a queue learns to stop registering.
- If customers want to buy against a Microsoft or AWS commitment and the reseller is authorized, set up reseller-led private offers. Check current marketplace terms and date them in your model.

## Days 61–90: Independence and review

**Milestone: the partner runs a demo and technical evaluation without your SE.**

- Your SE moves from leading meetings to reviewing them.
- Weekly pipeline calls become a monthly pipeline review.
- Day-90 review with both sponsors, ending in one decision: continue, re-plan, or exit.

| Day-90 measure | Green | Amber | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certified sellers / technical staff | 2 / 2 | 2 / 1 | Fewer |
| Approved registrations | 3+ | 1–2 | 0 |
| Partner-sourced qualified pipeline | At or above €<target> | Below target | Nothing qualified |
| Joint accounts with a dated next step | 8+ | 4–7 | Under 4 |
| Due diligence, MDF proof, registration hygiene | All current | One item overdue | Any red flag |

Thresholds are starting points. Set them against your cycle length. Report partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline separately, on definitions agreed with RevOps. Influenced never goes into the sourced total.

## Red flags to escalate

- Extra-discount requests with no competitive reason, especially on public-sector deals
- Requests to pay fees or commissions into a third-country account
- MDF claims without proof of performance
- Pressure to share contact-level data before the agreement covers it

Pause the deal or payment and send the file to counsel.

## What I need from you

Your typical deal size and sales cycle in Germany, whether you have direct reps in DACH, whether this reseller buys from you or through a distributor, and whether it sells mainly to Mittelstand, enterprise, or the public sector. Those set the day-90 targets. A closed deal inside 90 days is realistic only with a short cycle. Otherwise, judge the partner on certification, registrations, and qualified pipeline, and track days to first close for each recruit cohort.
